One Team, One Dream
What Makes Us Unique
Our Senior Leadership Team & Staff
Our aim is to develop well-balanced 16 year olds, ready to go out into the wider world, to lead happy and fulfilling lives and to contribute, positively and generously. We place great importance on high quality relationships, teamwork and a ‘can do attitude’.
Learning and wider school life at Patcham High doesn’t just take place between 8:30am and 3pm. We offer an extensive extra-curricular club’s programme across many subject areas.
At Patcham High School, our pastoral system aims to support the personal, social, and emotional development of every student, ensuring they feel safe, valued, and ready to learn.
Our Community

Thank you to our wonderful PTA who organised and ran this event today for our school community on the Patcham High field. A big shout out especially to Lousia, Zoe, Maya, Claire and Michelle. Thanks also to all those who attended and made the event a success.
13th Sep 2026 / Instagram
The @amazesussex @brightonstorytrail is here! We’re delighted to reveal that Patcham High School’s sculpture has found its home at Patcham Library. https://amazesussex.org.uk/sculptures/our-place/ Designed and decorated by a wonderful group of our students, the bench tells the story of Patcham. Follow the branches of the Klimt-inspired tree to spot links to our local area, including the South Downs and the Chattri, with the growing tree representing the personal growth of our students. On the other side, you’ll find Brighton Beach – complete with a Patcham High murmuration in the sky! Find our sculpture: Patcham Library Explore: Follow the Story Trail around Brighton & Hove to discover all the sculptures Launch: Saturday 12 September, 11am, Pavilion Gardens Fundraising: We’re aiming to raise £750 for Amaze Sussex, supporting families with disabled children and young people across Sussex. We’d love to see our students, families and wider Patcham community out exploring the trail. If you find our bench, take a photo and tag us! Support our fundraising for Amaze Sussex via the link in our bio: https://www.justgiving.com/page/patcham-high-school-storytrail #PatchamHighSchool #AmazeSussex #AmazeStoryTrail #BrightonAndHove #Patcham #OneTeamOneDream
11th Sep 2026 / Instagram
We are looking forward to welcoming prospective families to Patcham High School for our Open Evening and Open Morning Events over the next month. Please do share with families you know who may be interested.
11th Sep 2026 / Instagram
It was wonderful to see so many Patcham High students, families and staff out this weekend at Preston Park parkrunuk, especially given the heat! What a special community we have. We were so impressed by those running for the first time too. Thank you to all those who have already contributed or sponsored someone towards our fundraising campaign for new minibuses, we are very grateful. Link in bio if you’re able to help. #TeamPHS
21st Jun 2026 / Instagram
Midsummer Mayhem, the 90's musical Prepare for a festival of fun and frivolity hitting our stage on 16th and 17th July. Tickets on sale now through parent pay.
19th Jun 2026 / Instagram
This Wednesday 17th June is National #ThankaTeacherDay! There’s still time to show your appreciation by sending a FREE personalised limited-edition e-card to a member of our school staff who has made a difference to you, your child or our school community. A simple message of thanks can mean so much. Send yours now via @thankateacheruk / thankateacher.co.uk !
15th Jun 2026 / Instagram
We are excited to launch our fundraising campaign to help purchase new school minibuses, an investment that will benefit students across every year group and enrich school life for years to come. Our minibuses play a vital role in supporting the many opportunities that take learning beyond the classroom. From sports fixtures, educational visits and music events to Duke of Edinburgh expeditions, enrichment clubs, volunteering projects and university visits, new, modern minibuses will allow more students to participate in experiences that build confidence, independence and aspiration. To launch our fundraising efforts, we invite students, families, staff and the wider school community to run, jog or walk to take part in our Sponsored Park Run Weekend at Preston Park. Every step will help us move closer to our goal. Saturday 20th June: 5K Park Run or Sunday 21st June: 2K Park Run. (Don't forget to sign up for a barcode through Park Run so you can record your time!) We are also delighted to open this campaign to the wider community: Local businesses, organisations, former students, friends and supporters will be able to contribute through our crowdfunder webpage, where we will publicly recognise and thank donors for their generosity and support. If local businesses or individuals are able to make any significant contributions and would like to do this to the school directly for this campaign rather than via the crowdfunder, please contact finance@patchamhigh.org.uk. Please do share - the link is in our bio. Thank you!
14th Jun 2026 / Instagram
The Art rooms have been a hive of activity over the past couple of weeks with Year 11 students sitting their 10 hour Art exams. I wish we could share their work with you but we have to wait until after their grades are awarded over the summer - but I can assure you they will be worth the wait! In the meantime, here is our Artwork of the week featuring three of our wonderful Y8 students - Djoumana, Sofia and Joe.
8th May 2026 / Instagram
Student voice matters. Patcham High School is encouraging all students to take part in The Big Future, a national survey led by the @childrenscommissioner . The survey asks young people about: Their hopes for the future The changes they want to see in their communities The issues that matter most to them What a good childhood should look like today With more young people set to be eligible to vote in future elections, this is an important opportunity for children and young people to share their views and help shape future decisions. The survey is open to all children and young people. Complete the survey here: childrenscommissioner.gov.uk/thebigfuture or use the QR code. The Big Future Survey #StudentVoice #TheBigFuture #PatchamHighSchool #YouthVoice
8th May 2026 / Instagram
Our Year 10 Citizenship GCSE pupils had an amazing visit to Brighton Law Courts, where they watched real cases and explored the Magistrates’ Court! ⚖️ A fantastic hands-on experience that brought their learning to life and will help them prepare for their exams.
7th May 2026 / Instagram
Year 10 students visited the University of Sussex Engineering Department for a full day of workshops. They had the opportunity to see where the Formula Sussex racing team designs, builds, and tests their cars. The students also took part in hands-on activities, including testing metal loads, CAD design, electronics, and using a racing simulator. It was a fantastic day, and we would like to thank the @sussexuni for hosting us!
5th May 2026 / Instagram
We wanted to give a huge shoutout to Clare and the parent/carer volunteer team who manage our pre-loved uniform. They have raised a staggering £1735.40 which goes towards boosting our literacy work across school. We are so grateful to them and to all the families who have contributed. Our next pre-loved sale will take place on Friday 3rd July (Transition Day).
5th May 2026 / Instagram
A group of our Year 9 students embarked on a journey to uncover the endless possibilities of a career in the NHS! Through online webinars and in-school activities, they discovered their strengths and passions, and began to envision a future where they can make a real difference.
23rd Mar 2026 / Instagram
Look at these beautiful creations from our Year 8 artists as part of their Marine Life project. Students studied the work of @yellenajames and took inspiration from it to create their own artwork.
22nd Mar 2026 / Instagram
More World Book Day Celebrations at Patcham High Students were tasked with creating a piece of art (in any form) inspired by a book they love. From crochet, to painting, to songwriting and much more... Here you can see some of the wonderful outcomes - so much creativity. Well done to everyone who took part!
5th Mar 2026 / Instagram
World Book Day arrived early at Patcham High School We did briefly consider holding our Year 8 Meet the Teacher evening with staff dressed as book characters… but thought celebrating a day early might be the safer option! There was a brilliant turnout from staff dressing up as characters from their favourite books. Can you guess which book the Maths and Science departments chose?! Students also took part in a shared reading experience, with a short story read in lessons across all subjects throughout the day. Our library was buzzing at break and lunchtime with activities, and students have also attended assemblies this week which shared staff reading journeys (including some excellent childhood photos!). A great way to celebrate reading, imagination and the power of a good story. #WorldBookDay #LoveReading #PatchamHigh #ReadingForPleasure
5th Mar 2026 / Instagram
A very warm welcome to the students and families who’ve been offered a place at Patcham High School today. We’re delighted you’ll be joining our community. We know starting secondary school is a big step, and our transition programme is built around what research tells us works best: working in partnership with families and primary schools. Providing early opportunities to connect with and build relationships with our staff, clear routines and expectations, strong communication with families, and support that builds confidence from the very beginning. You’ll receive information from us soon about next steps and transition activities, in the meantime, do check out our website. We look forward to getting to know you. #NationalOfferDay #WelcomeToPatcham #Year7Transition #PatchamHighSchool
2nd Mar 2026 / Instagram
Join Our Community at Patcham High School Thinking about your child's next step… or yours? Looking for a vibrant place to work, learn, or connect? Our Join Us section has everything you need in one place. - Why Patcham High School: links useful areas of our website for prospective families - Admissions: links to Brighton and Hove admissions informaiton - Prospectus: Browse our online prospectus and watch our school video showcasing so much of what we have to offer. - Year 6-7 Transition: Will continue to be updated over the course of the year with important information for our new Year 7 families. - Open Events: Dates and information about our Open Events will be published here - Work With Us: Information about joining our staff team, including any current vacancies. - Hire our Facilities: From sports spaces to event venues, our facilities are available for hire. Visit the Join Us page on our website to explore opportunities to become part of our community. #JoinUs #PatchamHighSchool #SecondarySchoolJourney
2nd Mar 2026 / Instagram
Loved being able to see these talented footballers play on the 3G at the end of term. National Cup Round 2 winners for our U15 females.
27th Feb 2026 / Instagram
We've given our defibs the best chance of saving a life! We’re proud to share that all four defibrillators at Patcham High School are now registered on The Circuit, the national defibrillator network run by the British Heart Foundation. The Circuit maps defibrillators across the UK, allowing ambulance services to locate the nearest registered device when a bystander calls 999 in response to an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. #PatchamHighSchool #TheCircuit #EverySecondCounts
27th Feb 2026 / Instagram
Hear From Our Students
The best thing about Patcham is the support from the teachers. They genuinely care and always give advice that helps me do my best.
I really enjoyed studying The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde and I think I enjoyed it more due to how we were taught it. I like to hear other people’s interpretations and how they dissect a story. My English lessons help me read more challenging books.
Patcham High is fun, friendly and full of brilliant people. It’s been great to have lessons taught by subject specialists and the there’s been a huge range of sports of offer.
Patcham High is full of great opportunities with so many clubs to attend.
I want to be an author, and my lessons help my writing be the best it can be.
Studying geography at Patcham High sparked my interest in how landscapes form, but it was a field trip to the Jurassic Coast that became a pivotal moment. Seeing the rivers and rock layers up close made me realise this was something I wanted to understand more deeply — it’s what led me to become a geomorphologist.
Ellie C, Leaver 2013

pageCache.pageTitle: Brighton Magistrate Inspires Citizenship GCSE Students - News - Patcham High School
pageCache.text:
Brighton Magistrate Inspires Citizenship GCSE Students
Robert Macrowan, Justice of the Peace, recently visited our GCSE Citizenship classes to deliver two insightful sessions on law and the role of magistrates in the UK legal system.
Magistrates play a vital role in administering justice, making important decisions in both criminal and family courts. Their work helps to protect, support, and improve the lives of people within their communities.
'Hearing directly from a magistrate brought the law to life for our students. It was an inspiring opportunity to understand the real-world impact of justice in our community.'
The workshops were both engaging and inspiring, giving students a deeper understanding of how justice is delivered at a local level. The classes are now eagerly looking forward to visiting Brighton Law Courts in the new year, where they will experience the workings of the courtroom first-hand.
It was really interesting to learn how magistrates make such important decisions that affect people’s lives. It made me even more excited to visit the courts and see justice in action!”
GCSE Citizenship Student

pageCache.pageTitle: Meet Our Senior Leadership Team - Patcham High School
pageCache.text:
Meet Our Senior Leadership Team
A group of dedicated, experienced professionals committed to ensuring the highest standards of education and care.
Our Senior Leadership Team leads with clarity and compassion, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and inclusion. With a strong focus on teaching and learning, student wellbeing, and staff development, they drive the school forward and ensure that every decision is made with our students' best interests at heart. They are visible, approachable, and deeply committed to working in partnership with students, families, and staff.
John is Headteacher at Patcham High School. He holds a BA (Hons) Degree from the London School of Economics, as well as a Postgraduate Certificate in Education and a Master’s Degree from the Institute of Education. Before his career in teaching, John served in The Parachute Regiment. He has since taught in schools across London and West Sussex and is a qualified Advanced Skills Teacher. He holds the National Professional Qualification for Headship (NPQH) and the National Professional Qualification for Executive Leadership (NPQEL). Alongside his headship, John holds an interim appointment with Brighton & Hove City Council as Lead Strategic Education Consultant, providing strategic leadership and advice across the full breadth of the Central Hub’s Tier 2 and Tier 3 Alternative Provision.
Mike is a Deputy Headteacher at Patcham High School. He holds a BA (Hons) Degree in Geography from Bath Spa University as well as a Postgraduate Certificate in Education from Goldsmiths, University of London. Before his career in teaching, Mike worked in the Financial services sector. He has since taught in schools in London, Thailand and Kent. He also holds the National Professional Qualification for Headship.​
Mark is a Deputy Headteacher at Patcham High School. He holds a BA (HONS) Degree from London Metropolitan University, as well as a Postgraduate Certificate in Education and a Master’s Degree from the University of Sussex. Before his career in teaching, Mark was a qualified heating engineer. He trained in schools across London and is a qualified Advanced Skills Teacher. He also holds the National Professional Qualification for Headship.
Assistant Headteachers
Ruth is an Assistant Headteacher at Patcham High School. She gained a BSc Degree from Royal Holloway, University of London in Mathematics and Psychology, before completing her Postgraduate Certificate in Education and Master’s in Education from the University of Sussex. She is a qualified Advanced Skills Teacher and completed her second Master’s in Education Leadership and Management. Prior to working at Patcham, Ruth taught at schools in East Sussex and London. She is currently completing her National Professional Qualification for Headship. ​
Patrick is an Assistant Headteacher at Patcham High School. He has a degree in Sport, Physical Education and Coaching Sciences from the University of Birmingham, as well as a PGCE in Physical Education from the University of Chichester and also holds a Master’s degree in Education from the University of Sussex, which focused on the importance of shared agency over children’s learning. Patrick has previously worked at schools in West Sussex and Brighton.
Mary is an Assistant Headteacher, the Designated Safeguarding Lead, Designated Teacher, and Director of Alternative Provision at Patcham High School. She holds a BA (Hons) in English from the University of Kent, a Postgraduate Certificate in Education, and a Master’s degree from the University of Sussex.
Rachael is an Assistant Headteacher at Patcham High School. She gained her teaching qualification at Liverpool John Moores University studying Mathematics Education. Rachael taught at schools in Liverpool and West Sussex prior to joining Patcham High School. Since joining she has become a qualified Advanced Skills Teacher and was the Head of Mathematics for several years. She has recently completed her Master’s in Business Administration.
Bex is SENCO at Patcham High School. She holds a BSc (Hons) Degree from the University of Keele in Psychology and Education. She completed a Certificate of Higher Education in Mathematics before going on to complete her PGCE in Secondary Mathematics at the University of Brighton. Bex went on to gain a Master’s in Education from the University of Brighton, and completed her National Award in SEN Co-ordination in January 2025 via the University of Chichester. Prior to working as a SENCO, Bex spent 7 years as a Head of Year and is also a fully qualified Youth Mental Health First Aider.
Tom is Director of Sport at Patcham High School. He holds a BSc in Sports, Health and Exercise Science from St Mary's University in Twickenham. He gained his qualified teacher status via the Graduate Teaching Programme (GTP) which he completed at the University of Sussex in 2010/11. He holds coaching qualifications in a number of different sports including Cricket, Rugby and Football. Prior to working at Patcham High School Tom taught in schools in London.
Josie is Director of Science at Patcham High School. She gained a BSc (Hons) Degree from University College London in Medicinal Chemistry before completing her Postgraduate Certification in Education at the Institute of Education, University of London. Prior to working at Patcham, Josie has taught at schools in London and worked in Marketing and HR in the IT industry.
Kerry is Director of Student Support at Patcham High School. She holds a BA (hons) degree in English with Qualified Teacher Status, and has been the qualified Senior Mental Health Lead since 2022. Kerry joined Patcham in 2012 and during this time has been a Head of Year, seeing a year group through their full five years at Patcham, Director of the Bridge (mat. cover) before becoming the Director of Student Support, a role responsible for Attendance and Mental Health across the school.
Holly is Director of English at Patcham High School. She holds a BA (Hons) Degree in English Literature and Postgraduate Certification in Education from the University of Sussex. Before working at Patcham High School, Holly worked at a school in London, leaving as Literacy Lead. She was then a leader in an international school, enriching her practice by teaching a range of qualifications including the International Baccalaureate, multiple A Level courses and GCSEs across different exam boards.
Emma is Director of Maths at Patcham High School. She gained her BSc in Mathematics from the University of Manchester. Prior to qualifying as a teacher, she worked as a Consumer and Market Analyst and within the charitable sector. Emma has taught in schools in Brighton and East Sussex, before joining the Maths department at Patcham in 2016.
Jo has a Master’s in Business Administration from the Open University. Joanne has AAT level 4 accountancy qualifications and a Professional Diploma in Management. She has worked as Bursar and School Business Manager in schools in East Sussex and Brighton since 2014. Prior to this she worked for Thomson Reuters for 20 years and was head of operations in a social media agency.

Jo has a Master’s in Business Administration from the Open University. Joanne has AAT level 4 accountancy qualifications and a Professional Diploma in Management. Patcham Partnership Events
We place high value on strong partnerships with families, and our regular reporting and partnership evenings are key to that connection.
Through clear, accessible communication, we keep you informed about your child’s academic progress, achievements, and next steps. Partnership Events such as Meet the Teacher evenings are opportunities for meaningful dialogue with teachers, where successes are celebrated, targets are set, and support plans are refined. We see these conversations as part of a shared journey — working together to ensure every child reaches their full potential.
Patcham Partnership Evenings
Each Year group will have one Meet the Teacher evening per year where families will have the opportunity to book 5 minute slots with your child’s teachers.
All Meet the Teacher evenings will run face to face and be held in the school from 4pm to 7pm
Bookings will be made via EduLink One with families able to specific slots approximately 2 weeks before.
The dates for each year group are scheduled across the year to gain the maximum benefit from the consultations for both staff and families. Specific dates are published on the school calendar with families able to filter by Year group.
In the Autumn term Year 7 families will have an additional opportunity for an individual meeting with their child’s form tutor face to face towards the end of the first half term to support the transition process.
Years 8, 9, 10 and 11 families will be invited to a Securing Success and Meet the Tutor Evening event. To find out how we can work in partnership to support your child this year followed by an opporunity to meet your child's tutor.

To coincide with the full report home
To coincide with the GCSE option choices
Midpoints of the first year of GCSE courses

Student Progress Reports
Each student will receive two reports per year. One of these reports will be a ‘progress’ check which is a brief summary of the latest assessments taken for each subject, attitude to learning and homework scores, achievement points and attendance summary. The second report is a full report for each subject including all of the latest assessment and attendance information as well as comments from individual teachers for every subject.
In Years 7 to 9, reporting refers to student’s individual flightpaths. Students’ assessment results are allocated flightpaths that broadly equate to their progress and likely GCSE outcomes as shown in the graphic. The starting point of their progress is their Key Stage 2 (Year 6) SATs and their initial assessments in Year 7. Students may well move between flightpaths across different subjects and at different times within the Key Stage.
In Years 10 and 11, GCSE grades 9-1 are awarded for their assessments (flightpaths are no longer used). All reports will be uploaded to be viewed in EduLink One. Hard copies can be sent home on request. Reporting is generally released to Parents/Carers in time to coincide with consultation evenings.

Celebration as Patcham High School Students Shine in GCSE Results
Students at Patcham High School are celebrating this year’s GCSE results with an atmosphere of pride throughout the school community.
Results have improved across the board, with more students achieving top grades and more securing overall passes than in previous years. The school's pass rate was 8% above the national average, bucking the national trend and underlining the hard work of students, staff and families.
I am incredibly proud of our students and absolutely thrilled with these results. They show not only academic strength but also the dedication, resilience and creativity of our young people. We’re proud of every single achievement, whether that’s top grades or personal progress.
John McKee, Headteacher
A quarter of all Patcham High grades, over 400 individual results, were awarded at grades 9–7 (the equivalent of A*/A), reflecting a meaningful rise in top outcomes.
Among the individual successes were students who made significant personal progress during their time at the school as well as those who achieved exceptional grades across a wide range of subjects.
We are delighted to see our students heading on to sixth forms, colleges, apprenticeships and training, with these results opening doors to exciting futures.
Mike Newman, Deputy Head
For the second year running, more students at Patcham High are achieving excellent results in Modern Foreign Languages, a notable success given that numbers nationally have been in decline. Results in creative and performance subjects including art, drama, music and dance, are also thriving with many students securing strong grades in these areas.
There was a wonderful atmosphere in the school hall as students collected their results, with families and teachers on hand to share in the celebrations. Smiles, hugs and even a few happy tears marked the occasion.
Ruth Astley, Assistant Head
A selection of photographs from the morning reflects the excitement and joy of this special day.

One Voice Partnership Statement
One Voice Partnership statement
Communities across Brighton & Hove stand together as One Voice
Following the terrorist incident at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in Crumpsall, Manchester this morning, the city’s One Voice Partnership strongly condemns this act of violence, targeting of a synagogue, and our Jewish communities.
The Brighton & Hove ‘One Voice Partnership’ reaffirms that we stand together with our Jewish communities and stand together against antisemitism.
We do not tolerate violence against innocent people, wherever it takes place. Together we speak with one voice against extremist perspectives and terrorist actions.
Mahir Chowdhury, the Chair of the Racial Harassment Forum said: “The incident has deeply shocked and saddened us all. We send our heartfelt sympathies to the families of those who have lost their loved ones, those who have been injured, and all our Jewish communities. Our thoughts and prayers are with the victims, their families, and our Jewish Communities.”
Sabri Ben-Ameur from the Brighton & Hove Muslim Forum said: "We stand in solidarity with Jewish communities in our city and strongly condemn this act of terrorism against the Hebrew Congregation Synagogue, in Manchester on Yom Kippur, the holiest days for Jewish people.”
“We urge all in our city, of faith and no-faith, to respect and uphold the sanctity of places of worship and Holy days.”
Anthea Ballam, Chair of Brighton & Hove Interfaith Contact Group stated: "Sadly, the threat from terrorism and the threat to our Jewish communities are both real."
"We stand firm that these threats and acts of violence, antisemitism, and hate must stop.”
“We will continue our fundamental commitment of unity and respect for all those of faith and none in our city.”
Councillor Bella Sankey, Leader of Brighton & Hove City Council added: "To target Jewish people during Yom Kippur, such a sacred day for the Jewish people across the world, is heartbreaking. The rise of antisemitism in recent years is unacceptable and my thoughts are with everyone affected, and with the wider Jewish community who will be feeling the impact of this violence and violation. We will do all we can to keep our Jewish community safe."
Jess Gibbons, the council's Chief Executive and the chair of the One Voice Partnership said: "The council, together with the One Voice Partnership, will work to promote our city values of respect for all, fairness, equality, and diversity. We reject any attempt to divide, threaten or commit acts of violence in our communities."
“Places of worship serve important role for our communities and faith communities should not have to worry about being targeted for who they are.”
“Our Jewish community should be able to feel safe to practice and demonstrate faith without the threat of terrorism, violence, or hostility.”
The police and other agencies continue to work to keep the public safe. You can find a statement from police: https://www.counterterrorism.police.uk/declaration-of-a-terrorist-incident-in-manchester/
Threat from UK to all forms of terrorism remains at Substantial (meaning an attack is likely) and has remained such since February 2022.
The threat of individuals acting on their own, inspired by their online activity or by other groups or causes is part of the current terrorist threat in the UK. Residents should remain vigilant and report any suspicious activity to the police.
Reporting suspicious activities
Co-operation between the public and the police is the greatest asset in tackling the challenge the UK faces from terrorism.
Sussex Police and Brighton & Hove City Council ask our residents and communities to remain aware and to report any suspicious behaviour or activity immediately by calling 999 in an emergency or the confidential anti-terrorist hotline on 0800 789 321
You can use online form to report suspicious or terrorist activity: How to report possible terrorist activity | Metropolitan Police
Report illegal terrorist information, pictures or videos you’ve found on the internet.
Further resources: Action Counters Terrorism (ACT) and Prevent on the council website.
Reporting hate incidents and seeking support
Everyone in Brighton & Hove has a right to feel safe. One Voice members urge everyone to be aware and encourage residents and communities to report any racist, religiously motivated, and all forms of hate incidents within our communities.
Our community safety casework team works closely with the police and our communities to prevent anti-social behaviour and hate incidents and support people affected.
If you have been a victim of a hate incident, our community safety team are here to support you and provide advice. You can contact our team by:
If you are worried or concerned about how the incident has affected you or any of your communities, please do advise Prevent Lead Officer on Channel.Prevent@brighton-hove.gov.uk and we will ensure that together with other statutory partners we will respond to community concerns.
The council has pledged to be an anti-racist council and our anti-racism strategy sets out how we will use our resources and change what we do to actively dismantle racist structures and challenge racial inequality.
You can also find an initial statement from the leader of the council here: Statement on Manchester synagogue attack
Email: communitysafety.casework@brighton-hove.gov.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Royal Institution Science Show - News - Patcham High School
pageCache.text:
Royal Institution Science Show
Patcham High was buzzing with excitement yesterday as we welcomed the Royal Institution for a spectacular day of science shows.
We were delighted to host the “Explosive Food” science show, which explored just how fascinating everyday food can be through brilliant demonstrations and plenty of student participation. The show linked perfectly to our curriculum, particularly our Year 8 food and nutrition topic, and helped pupils make meaningful connections between what they learn in class and real-world science. Students watched jelly babies set on fire and saw the digestive system recreated in all its messy glory,
In the evening, we were delighted to host a special community show for families and children from across the city, giving even more young people the chance to experience the fun, energy and wonder of real-world science. There were imploding drink cans, homemade rockets, the tablecloth trick and even an experiment proving that a two books can be stronger than twelve children combined! Students learned about the science behind rockets and the key components needed to make one launch successfully. Opportunities like this are incredibly valuable in showing how important science is in everyday life, sparking curiosity, and strengthening our connections with families.
A huge thank you Georgia Egner, our Lead Practitioner in Science for making this event happen, to the Royal Institution for inspiring our next generation of scientists and to everyone who attended for making the event such a memorable celebration of curiosity and discovery.

Careers (CEIAG) & Post-16 Progression
We believe our students are never too young to start thinking about and preparing for their future.
We aim to make sure students are given the opportunity to equip themselves with the self-confidence and resilience to manage the decisions they will need to make to shape their future working lives and deal effectively with the challenges of transition. Careers Information, Education, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) is an essential part of this process, so we ensure that all our learners get access to a programme of careers education from Year 7 to Year 11 that is relevant and aspirational.
Utilising ‘Gatsby Benchmarks’ to develop and improve our careers programme we continually look for opportunities to collaborate with outside facilitators to ensure we offer relevant and up to date advice and guidance. We ensure that our students gain important experiences and skills from meeting and working with a range of education / training providers and employers. We use Compass+ as our school self evaluation tool, looking at provision and impact across all year groups, reviewed annually with our external Careers Mentor. Students at Patcham High are empowered to make informed decisions which are aspirational and appropriate for them. Students benefit from career focussed activities designed to develop social skills, grit, and resilience and for them to be informed and aspirational when considering their futures.
Our careers programme is driven by these core documents:
DfE: Careers guidance and access for education and training providers
https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/careers-guidance-provision-for-young-people-in-schools/careers-guidance-and-access-for-education-and-training-providers
Gatsby: Good Career Guidance
Mrs Moore is our Careers Advisor. She works in the school to maximise opportunities for students to engage in university trips, work experience and college courses alongside their GCSE studies, with an emphasis on increasing students understanding and raising aspirations and awareness of different progression routes post 16.
Mrs Moore works closely with local employers, universities and colleges to provide an enriched timetable for students both in school and offsite. She also delivers careers guidance, inspiring and supporting students with the choices they need to empower them to develop confidence in their own ability to research the options open to them. A wide range of providers and employers deliver information sessions to students in year group assemblies, careers education workshops and employer engagement sessions.
PHS-provider-access-policy-statement.pdf
PHS-Careers-Policy.pdf
Year 10 Work Experience
Year 10 work experience week is a crucial feature of Key Stage 4 CEIAG and is bespoke to every student. Mrs Moore also provides 1:1 careers guidance interviews that are personalised, comprehensive and impartial.
External careers advice is facilitated through the National Careers Service
If you require any further information please email Mrs Mooreamoore@patchamhigh.org.uk or call 01273 543494.
Useful Careers Information
Expand the following sections below to find out more...
Year 9 GCSE options – For information on where your subject can take you visit the following websites:
For general support with choosing GCSE options:
Every effort is made by all staff at Patcham High to secure the most appropriate destination for all our students post 16. All students have the opportunity for an individual Careers Information and Advice meeting with our career advisor, Mrs Moore.
GCSEs are Level 2 courses. Once GCSEs have been completed, students can progress to Level 3 qualifications.
After Year 11, Patcham High students can choose from a variety of options, including:
2-year courses, usually 3–4 subjects, assessed mostly through exams.
Entry requirements: 5 GCSEs at grade 4+, some subjects need a 6
Combines working in a real job with studying for a qualification (Level 2–5). Can be started at 16+. Great for hands-on learners.
Level 2 Apprenticeship: Preferred GCSEs grade 3s English & Maths - Potential to retake alongside if grades are lower than a 3.
Level 3 Apprenticeship: GCSE English & Maths grade 4+
2-year courses, usually 3 subjects Practical, work-related courses, assessed by coursework and some exams – can be combined with A levels,
Entry requirements: usually 5 GCSEs at 4+, incl. English & Maths
Stepping-stone courses → build skills before moving on.
Foundation Courses are usually Entry Level (Entry 1, 2 or 3) or Level 1 (below GCSE grade 4).
They sit below Level 2 (GCSEs) and are designed to prepare learners for GCSEs, Functional Skills, BTECs, T Levels or apprenticeship
In English or maths - focused on practical skills needed for work and daily life. Often done alongside vocational courses
2-year courses, mix of classroom learning and 45-day industry placement
Entry requirements: usually 5 GCSEs at 4+, incl. English & Maths
You can find links to all the colleges in the area, information on when they have their open events, and useful links in the following document:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1oQNZVKkDI73AYyAZMtRPYAlqG3X2_aXxuEF9SUQOaXQ/edit?tab=t.0

Applying for an apprenticeship is the same as applying for a job but with the understanding that you will learn on the go, for instance by going to college one day a week or doing virtual training once a month. You usually need to fill in an application form or CV, answer some questions, and maybe do an interview or small tests. If you get accepted, you’ll start working and training at the same time, often with extra support if you need it.
It’s important to apply to college as well as apprenticeships because apprenticeships are competitive and you might not get one straight away. Having a college place means you still have a safe backup option so you can continue learning and working towards your goals while you keep applying for apprenticeships.

Albion Stars Bring Joy to Patcham High
What began as a week of disappointment for 60 Patcham High students turned into a truly unforgettable moment, thanks to the Brighton & Hove Albion Foundation — and a surprise visit from two Premier League stars.
After a last-minute issue with transport meant the cancellation of a planned football trip to the Netherlands, spirits at the school were understandably low. But on Friday, students were treated to an inspiring coaching session from BHAFC Foundation coaches — and the unexpected arrival of Albion’s Joel Veltman and new signing Olivier Boscagli turned the day into something extraordinary.
The players took part in a Q&A, chatted with students, signed shirts and memorabilia, and posed for photos, creating an electric atmosphere and leaving smiles all around.
We were sorry to hear that the Patcham High trip had been cancelled, but hopefully the coaching session and our visit helped to make up for the disappointment. It was great to meet the pupils and teachers — and so many Albion fans!
The visit was a powerful reminder of the strength of the school community and the generosity of local partners. While not every plan from the original trip could be replaced, the school hopes this experience sparks further collaborations with BHAFC and other organisations, creating even more enriching opportunities in the future.
What began as a disappointing week turned into something truly special for our students. They absolutely loved the coaching session, and meeting Joel and Oli was just what they needed to end the week on a high. Both players were incredibly generous with their time — so kind, engaging, and down-to-earth. Our pupils were thrilled to ask questions, get autographs, and share their love of football. It’s a moment they’ll never forget.
Ruth Astley, Assistant Headteacher
The Netherlands trip is now being rescheduled for the autumn term, and in the meantime, the resilience, positivity and enthusiasm shown by students throughout the week is something the entire school can be proud of.
We are grateful to Brighton and Hove Albion First Team photographer James Boardman for sharing his photos.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lord Parry Mitchell Brings Politics to Life for Patcham High Citizenship Students - News - Patcham High School
pageCache.text:
Lord Parry Mitchell Brings Politics to Life for Patcham High Citizenship Students
GCSE Citizenship students at Patcham High School were given a unique insight into the world of politics and law this term, both through a fascinating visit to London and a visit from Lord Parry Mitchell.
As law and politics make up half of the GCSE Citizenship course, students recently travelled to the capital to see these subjects come to life in some of the UK’s most iconic venues.
The day began at the Supreme Court, where the students enjoyed a bespoke guided tour and learned about how the court serves as the final court of appeal for all UK civil and criminal cases. Students explored the traditional and historical courtrooms and heard how Justices decide cases of the greatest public and constitutional importance.
After a quick lunch in Parliament Square, and a competitive statue quiz they made their way to Westminster, the very heart of UK politics. They took a guided Tour of Parliament, visiting the House of Commons and House of Lords debating chambers, the division lobbies, Westminster Hall, Central Lobby and St. Stephen’s Hall. Students admired the architecture, symbolism and ceremony, and met The Rt Hon Lord Levy.
The highlight for many came when they were able to sit in the Public Gallery of the House of Lords to watch a live debate on the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill. Peers discussed the dangers of social media and the importance of all children having access to swimming lessons, prompting students to reflect on how fortunate they are to have a pool at Patcham High.
The day ended with a Power of Democracy workshop, where students created petitions on issues of national importance and reflected on how the public, MPs, Peers, Justices and the Monarch all play a role in shaping UK laws. Students were full of positive praise about the day:
“I loved that we could sit in the public gallery of the House of Lords and hear them debate about amendments of a bill. The Supreme Court was very interesting and I loved being able to sit in each courtroom and learn about the symbolism of everything.”
Isabelle, Y11 student
“I enjoyed listening to the history behind Parliament and looking around the House of Commons and Lords.”Sophia, Y11 Student
Building on this powerful experience, students were delighted to continue their exploration of Parliament back in the classroom when Lord Parry Mitchell visited Patcham High to speak about his experiences in the House of Lords.
Lord Mitchell spoke about his journey into Parliament, how laws are made, and the current legislation he is involved with, including the Online Safety Act, the Assisted Dying Bill, and his campaign to reform payday loans. The visit provided an inspiring opportunity for students to connect their classroom learning with real-life political debates.
Not only did Lord Mitchell share his knowledge of the House of Lords, he also spoke about the different ways of getting into Parliament which helped us think about routes we could take in the future. Toby, Y11 Student
“Meeting a Lord is a very special opportunity for our pupils. They were really interested in Lord Mitchell’s story which not only brought their GCSE Citizenship learning to life, it also showed them that they have the power to bring about the change they want to see in the world. His visit has demonstrated to our young people that politicians are everyday people, and I’m sure some of them can now picture themselves in his position one day.”
Hannah Kinchin-Frost, Head of Life Skills
At Patcham High, we are committed to providing opportunities that extend learning beyond the classroom and connect education to the wider world. Experiences like the London trip and Lord Mitchell’s visit not only strengthen students’ understanding of politics and citizenship, but also reflect our core values of Pride, Respect and Success through inspiring every young person to see themselves as active citizens who can help shape the future.

PE Teacher's end of term challenge to raise funds for local charities
One of our PE teachers, Matt Lindner is taking on an incredible challenge on the final day of this term by juggling a football for the 12 miles from the Amex Stadium all the way to Sussex FA HQ in Lancing.
He is hoping to raise £1,750, which will be split as follows:
£750 to Martlets, supporting their incredible work with individuals and families affected by cancer. A couple of close friends have sadly been lost to this awful illness, and I want to do whatever I can so that fewer people have to go through it.
£1,000 split three ways between the grassroots communities that have shaped so much of our lives:
– Sussex Schools FA, where I coach the U14s, helping to fund Finals Day on June 6th so every district gets the day they deserve.
– Mile Oak FC, where I’m part of the Vets and coach the U14s, and where Rhys has played for seven years.
– Southwick FC, where I manage the brilliant U12s and Owen has proudly played for the last three years.
Any support, whether a donation or simply sharing his page is gratefully received. Thank you for helping him make a real difference.
Any families able to support can do so by donating through the following link:

Patcham Students Cook Up Success with Free Mussels from Fish Heroes
This week, thanks to Mike Maier, our Food Tech teacher, our students took part in the Fish Heroes programme, receiving a generous delivery of free mussels for use in lessons. The initiative aims to help young people gain confidence in preparing and cooking fish, while broadening their understanding of sustainable seafood.
Students learned how to clean, prepare and cook fresh mussels, producing a range of dishes and developing valuable practical skills along the way.
Nothing went to waste, once the mussels were cooked, Laura Bissonnet, Technology & Art teacher used the cleaned shells in a creative art activity, creating beautiful paintings.
It was a memorable experience, and we look forward to taking part in more opportunities that support hands-on learning in the food curriculum.
